description: Synthetic, stdlib + NumPy toy: a holographic tensor network (7 boundary physical qubits, 3 tensor layers of 6/7/6, 2 bulk logical qubits) built as a working membrane. Measured: the encoding is an isometry, no single boundary qubit carries the bulk, the erasure threshold is 2 (worst case), a real least-squares decoder recovers the bulk with a noise-dependent threshold, and the overlap-recall gate fails honestly on non-orthogonal patterns (no threshold separates real from code-random; no collision detection). It is not a real quantum error-correcting code and not a real holographic duality. The repository documents measured behaviour and limits, including negative results.
title: tensor-membrane: a holographic tensor network as a membrane — bulk logical qubits encoded across boundary physical qubits, with a real erasure decoder and a hard overlap-recall test (synthetic)
